principalConclusion: ARA must represent progression, mastery evidence, sequence authority, pacing, review scheduling, item relationships, examples, scaffolding, segmentation and resumption as distinct but composable dimensions. Structural completion is not mastery; spacing is not interleaving; learner pacing is not unrestricted sequence control; and support availability is not the same as automatic fading.
recommendedPath: Preserve AraLearn structural completion, authored microsequences, learner pacing, manual reprises and interruption-safe resumption as a reference profile.
Accept the 36 P2 dimensions into the first taxonomy while keeping the first implementation selective.
Allow criterion-gated mastery only through explicit evidence basis, criterion version, scope, remediation, override and recheck policies.

Use shared control as the general design direction: authors define coherent structure and prerequisites; learners control pace and permitted choices; institutions and protocols may lock values explicitly.
Represent spacing through schedule, interval pattern, retention horizon, load budget, deferral and missed-review rules; do not choose a universal algorithm.
Represent interleaving separately and use it only for justified discrimination among confusable categories or as an explicit research condition.
Use worked examples and scaffolds more strongly for novices and complex tasks, but require transition to independent problem solving and reversible support.
Preserve meaningful segmentation and resumption context for fragmented mobile study without behavioral telemetry.
Defer adaptive mastery estimation, scheduling, branching, struggle detection and automatic fading to later product, research and architecture decisions.

deferredCandidates.reason: Mastery estimates require construct validity, evidence windows, calibration, transparency, contestability and governance.
The literature supports spacing but not one universally optimal algorithm; product and deployment constraints remain undecided.
Branching needs learner-control, adaptation, transparency, fallback and domain-valid evidence.
Behavioral signals do not automatically measure struggle and cannot be collected or interpreted without authorization.
Fading depends on valid expertise or criterion evidence; universal automatic removal is not supported.
Generative reentry support raises accuracy, privacy, offline and UX questions; deterministic context cues are sufficient for the first taxonomy.

rejectedOrNotRecommended: A universal mastery threshold or fixed number-correct rule.
Treating structural completion, time, persistence or number of attempts as mastery.
A universal hard prerequisite gate without remediation, override and appeal.
An undifferentiated learner-control setting that merges pace, order, review and practice authority.
Universal interleaving across domains or from the beginning of instruction.
A universal equal, expanding or fixed spacing interval.
A worked-examples-only sequence without independent problem solving.
Automatic support fading based on an unvalidated mastery or struggle estimate.
Removing essential problem information under the label of fading.
Punishing or interpreting review deferral in non-consequential personal study.
Inferring disengagement, expertise or difficulty from interruption duration or resume behavior.
A product claim of an optimal scheduler before architecture and evaluation.
risks: Combinatorial complexity across progression, sequence, review and support parameters.
Using mastery terminology without a valid evidence basis or stable scope.
Overpractice and non-completion under aggressive mastery thresholds.
Hard locks that deny autonomy, accessibility or due process.
Confounding spacing with interleaving or retrieval practice.
Review overload, coercive notifications and abandonment.
Worked examples becoming passive reception or persisting after expertise changes.
Scaffolding removal increasing cognitive load or creating inaccessible paths.
Interruption data becoming surveillance or an invalid engagement proxy.
Research comparisons failing because effective sequence and support states were not snapshotted.
decisionChangingUncertainties: Mastery thresholds and reassessment policies for adult worker-students and different domains.
Fair and interpretable evidence for progression from equivalent or transfer items.
Effects of soft versus hard prerequisites in self-directed and formal deployments.
Practical spacing schedules under mobile offline use, multiple courses and constrained study time.
Review load budgets and deferral policies that preserve retention without creating coercion.
Domains and learner states in which interleaving is beneficial, neutral or harmful.
Expertise-sensitive timing and fading of examples and scaffolds outside procedural STEM tasks.
Accessibility of complex examples, review queues and branching on modest smartphones.
Deterministic versus AI-assisted reentry support after long interruptions.
Institutional workload, instructor burden and completion effects of mastery profiles.
Transfer to Brazilian, Portuguese and other non-WEIRD educational contexts.
